quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: Can wind noise damage your hearing?

options.text: No, you get used to it easily.
Yes, it can cause permanent hearing damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: Which material best protects motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather and sturdy synthetic materials provide the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When riding in a group, how often should you check your mirrors?

options.text: All riders should check them frequently.
Only the lead rider should check them.
Do not check them often because they distract you.

questions.correctAnswerText: All riders should check them frequently.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, all riders should check their mirrors often to watch the riders behind them and make sure the group stays together.

questions.question: What should be your main concern when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.explanation: Protection is your first concern when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Zigzag to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings. Do not zigzag, as this is more dangerous.

questions.question: Before riding, you should check the throttle. What should it do when you release it?
questions.explanation: The throttle should snap back when you release it. The clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: What material should riding gloves be made of?
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar durable material for grip and protection.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, avoid sudden changes in speed or direction to prevent skids. Accelerate, shift, turn, and brake smoothly.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Hides you from other road users.
Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid hazards. Keep safe space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chances of a crash by:

options.text: Not using turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.

questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others, use clear signals, keep safe space around you, look ahead 12 seconds, and be ready to react to any hazard.

questions.question: When entering a turn, it is best to:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears during a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles going under 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: To be seen more easily by other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to help other drivers see you. This works any time of day.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. Also, the vehicle may block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible, use signals, keep safe space, look ahead 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready to react.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you maintain proper balance.
